name: Defensible Space / Crime Prevention Through Environmental Design
citation: Newman, O. (1972). Defensible space. Macmillan. / Jeffery, C.R. (1971). Crime prevention through environmental design. Sage.
rejection_rationale: Confounded by social variables (Merry, 1981 critique). Defensible Space/CPTED claims about environmental design reducing crime cannot be separated from the social dynamics of the communities inhabiting those spaces. The Pruitt-Igoe failure was social-economic, not architectural. Template coverage would require sociological variables outside the neural-mechanistic framework.
key_references: Merry, S.E. (1981). Defensible space undefended. Urban Affairs Quarterly, 16(4), 397-422.

function_form.function_form: Crime(x) = f(Opportunity(x), Guardianship(x), Target(x)); Guardianship ∝ Surveillance + Territoriality
predictions: Natural surveillance (windows facing public space) reduces crime ~25-30%
Territorial markers (fences, landscaping) reduce stranger intrusion ~40%

provenance.seminal_paper: Jeffery, C.R. (1971). Crime Prevention Through Environmental Design. Beverly Hills: Sage Publications.
provenance.secondary_paper: Newman, O. (1972). Defensible Space: Crime Prevention through Urban Design. New York: Macmillan.
provenance.predecessor: Urban renewal research (1960s); environmental design theory; situational crime prevention
provenance.historical_context: CPTED originated around 1960 when urban designers recognized that urban renewal strategies were risking the social frameworks necessary for community self-policing. C. Ray Jeffery coined the term CPTED and developed theoretical framework (1971). Oscar Newman developed the parallel 'Defensible Space' concept (1972) with similar objectives. Newman's approach achieved broader practical adoption in architecture and urban planning, with subsequent re-examination of Jeffery's work.
key_milestones: 1960: Recognition of urban renewal's social costs
1971: Jeffery's foundational CPTED book and theoretical framework
1972: Newman's Defensible Space framework and architectural application
1975-1985: Newman's approach gains broader adoption in design practice
1981: Merry's critique revealing social confounding variables
1980s-Present: International expansion and refinement of CPTED principles
influenced_by: Urban planners and social scientists observing renewal failures
provenance.current_status: foundational but contested; significant practical application despite empirical limitations
provenance.verification_notes: Seminal papers verified via academic databases. Jeffery (1971) and Newman (1972) publication dates confirmed. Historical context of urban renewal (1960) verified. Merry's 1981 critique located in Urban Affairs Quarterly. Current international CPTED Association status confirmed.
